title: File descriptor limit reached causing connection refused errors
symptoms: Logs: OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files. New HTTP connections failing with Connection refused. Application logs: socket.error: [Errno 24] Too many open files. cat /proc/$(pidof gunicorn)/limits shows max 1024 open files. lsof count: 1024.
root_cause: Connection objects to Redis and PostgreSQL were not being properly closed in exception handlers. Each unhandled exception in the request pipeline left a socket file descriptor open. Over 8 hours under normal traffic, the process accumulated 1024 open file descriptors (the default ulimit).
fix_applied: 1. Restarted gunicorn to clear descriptors. 2. Fixed all connection cleanup: used context managers (with db.connect() as conn:). 3. Increased system ulimit to 65536: ulimit -n 65536 in /etc/security/limits.conf. 4. Added fd monitoring: alert when process fd count > 800. 5. Used connection pool with explicit timeout and cleanup.
